precepts.why:
Cain “brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord”, and Abel brought “of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof.” “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect.” What happened to Cain and Abel physically is a foreshadowing of Jacob and Esau spiritually: one is chosen and one is not.

Paul explains it with Rebecca’s twins: “For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth”. Then: “As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” Cain was not rejected because he was wroth; that was ordained from the beginning. It is about election, the purpose God makes. He can make one vessel for one use and another vessel of wrath fitted for destruction.

Christians take “not of works” to mean the law need not be kept. What it tells us is that from the foundation God chose his elect. He still requires the works of the law, not the sacrificial law, but being clean and repented, to obtain the kingdom of heaven. When the first world was formed every nation was supposed to follow the laws, and judgment followed whoever did not. Cain’s rebellious nature showed itself, and it continues to this day in Esau.

People say God doesn’t hate, and they isolate “God is love.” But notice it says “as it is written”: it is in the Bible. It was written first in Malachi: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” Edom says, “We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”, and he did, in the Renaissance. But the Lord says, “They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” God lets him rise to power so that he can take him down.

And the Lord asked Cain, “Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” Remember that, because the same reason Cain hated Abel is the reason Esau hates Jacob today. It is the same spirit; only the name changes. “Satan” simply means adversary, one who obstructs and opposes. That is why everything they do is about us: they were made for that purpose, to obstruct and oppose us, because God purposed it from the beginning.

note.label: War of the Gods

precepts.why:
Wisdom says “that which is made with hands is cursed, as well it, as he that made it: he, because he made it; and it, because, being corruptible, it was called god.” We did not glorify the Lord; we went after vain imaginations, professed ourselves to be wise, made idolatrous images after the image of corruptible man, and then called them god. The thing made and its maker are both cursed.

Now go to Christ, who is also a maker: he made everything seen and unseen, in earth and in heaven. Paul asks, “Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?” It is a rhetorical question, because everything he made is in its perfect form and perfect order. The hummingbirds still go to the nectar, lions still chase the beasts, mothers still give suck to their young, the whales do not get out of the water to walk on land, and the water does not pass the bounds of the sand unless the Lord sends his angels in the storm. Everything is in perfect order except the twelve tribes of Israel. Keep my commandments that you may live, and we said no.

“Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?” Christ created both. Jacob and Esau came from the same mother and father, the same lump: one a vessel of honour, which we descend from, and the other a vessel of dishonour.

Then: “What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”. While Esau fulfils his role as God’s sword, the Lord lets him do what he was created for, and what he was created for is destruction. They are here to serve a purpose, and then the Lord is going to destroy them. Wipe your tears: the nations got to go.

So the war of the gods is this: the true Maker whose works stay in order, against the gods men make with hands, which are cursed with the men who made them.

note.label: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.why:
The only one that can destroy America is Christ when he returns, and Romans 9 shows why God raised her up at all: “For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.”

Pharaoh was over Egypt, and Egypt has long been destroyed. Pharaoh is a metaphor for Rome, and a metaphor for America today. Revelation calls the great city spiritually Sodom and Egypt, and that is Pharaoh right there.

God raised America up. Why? That he might show his power in her. All the technological advances America has, God allowed her to have. There is no nation, no country, that can match Babylon the Great; that is why they call it the great: it has the greatest technology of all nations. Christ says, I must show my power in you, because I am the only one that can take America out.

Then “and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.” When Christ finally takes them down, his name shall be declared throughout all the earth, because we are going to declare his real name, his true name. That is the vengeance of Isaiah 47: “I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.”

precepts.why:
Ishmael received a blessing: fruitful, multiplied exceedingly, “twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation.” But the word to Abraham was kings shall come out of thee, and the covenant goes to one son: “my covenant will I establish with Isaac.”

Paul explains it: “Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called.” Ishmael was born of the flesh, of Sarai’s plan, with no word from God ordaining it. “They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.”

And the word of promise is the very word spoken here: “At this time will I come, and Sara shall have a son.” Isaac, whom Sarah would bear at the set time in the next year, is the child of the promise, and the covenant is with him.

We’re the prophets of the Most High God, and our job is to tell you the truth. “Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid.” Somebody will say it’s not right for God to hate Esau. God made his decision; he’s God and you’re not. Paul is giving you a brief synopsis of God’s plan from Genesis; that’s what this whole chapter is about.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.” As it was true back then, when the Lord had mercy on Israel in the captivity under Egypt, Paul is bringing it up to his time. “So then it is not of him that willeth”: Esau can’t will himself to be the people of God, can’t will himself to be the Israelites. “Nor of him that runneth”: you can run around the earth, church after church, synagogue after synagogue, and say I’m a Christian, I’m the people of God. “But of God that sheweth mercy”: it’s God’s decision who he’s going to have mercy on.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: Why did Paul go from Jacob and Esau to Moses and Pharaoh? He’s comparing Jacob and Esau to Egypt, bringing it up to his time, when the Israelites were under Roman domination. “Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up”: did not God raise up Pharaoh to be the world’s superpower? In Paul’s time the world’s superpower was Rome, and today it’s the United States of America. America is the new Pharaoh; Esau Edom is the new Pharaoh. The book Modern Judaism (1830) says ‘the descendants of Esau the sworn enemies of the descendants of Jacob even to the end of the world’, that they ‘subjugated Italy, founded Rome and the Roman Empire’, ‘professing the religion of Jesus of Nazareth’, and ‘hold the dominion over all Europe’. The scholars know Esau is Rome, and that the prophecies against Edom in Isaiah, Jeremiah and Obadiah have not yet received their full accomplishment.

“That I might shew my power in thee”: he would raise Esau up to such a level only God can take him down, just as when we were in Egypt only God could take down ancient Egypt. There are roughly 750 U.S. military bases outside of America, spread across 80 nations, three times as many as all other countries combined, with combatant commands in Africa, the Middle East, Europe and the Indo-Pacific. That’s why when black people say let’s get guns and overthrow them, be quiet; you ain’t overthrowing nothing. Their military has worldwide coverage. “And that my name might be declared throughout all the earth”: everybody is going to declare the name throughout the whole earth.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy”: meaning Israel, Jacob. “And whom he will he hardeneth”: he’s going to harden Esau. Paul is still on the same topic. He speaks with words hard to be understood, and Christians go, why’d he start talking about Jacob and Esau, Esau have I hated, then go to Pharaoh? He’s letting you know Esau would be the new Pharaoh.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “For who hath resisted his will?” Everybody does what God wants. “Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God?” Who in the hell are you to reply against your maker, your creator, with your ashy lips? “Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?” How could Esau jump up now and go, why have you made me this way? And some of our own people, when we say you’re the greatest nation on Earth, go no, we gotta be like everybody else; but God says you’re the top.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour”: out of Rebecca he made two. One vessel unto honour, which was Jacob, “and another unto dishonour”: that vessel is Esau.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “The vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”: fitted means created to be destroyed. We already read in Isaiah 34 that his sword will come down upon Idumea, the people of his curse, and in Isaiah 63, who is this that cometh from Edom with dyed garments.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “That he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy”: that’s Israel, “which he had afore prepared unto glory”.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: Now Paul is going to break down the mercy, because the argument was the northern kingdom don’t get no mercy, because they were not doing animal sacrifice. “Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only”: not of Judah only, “but also of the Gentiles”. That throws Christians off right there; some of y’all Christians are sitting there going, gotcha. But the Gentiles are the outcasts of Israel. The scattered remnants of Israel and Judah are going to be gathered together.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “As he saith also in Osee”: Osee is the Greek for Hosea. “I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.” Paul is quoting the prophet Hosea, and Christians don’t like to go to the quotes because they get cut.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “There shall they be called the children of the living God.” Paul is quoting Hosea about Israel.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “Esaias also crieth concerning Israel”: Esaias is the Greek for Isaiah. “Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved”. Only a remnant of our people is going to be saved, brothers and sisters, only a remnant.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “For he will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth.” The Lord is going to make a short work on this Earth.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “And as Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed”: Sabaoth is the transliteration of the Hebrew word meaning hosts, armies, the Lord of armies or Lord of hosts. If the Lord didn’t leave a seed of Israelites to repent, all of us “had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha.” I know it’s a hard thing, but the word of God is meant for them to repent.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: We know who these Gentiles are according to Matthew 4:15 and Isaiah 11:10-12: the scattered Israelites, the outcasts of Israel, the dispersed of Judah. “The Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness”: those scattered Israelites were not brought up under the law of Moses and never heard about Christ; they were raised up under Gentile philosophies, Greek and Roman, just like our people today brought up under American Christian philosophies and Islamic philosophies. “Have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith”: which is Christ. The apostles and disciples went out teaching those Israelites scattered abroad.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness”: those scribes, Pharisees and Sadducees brought up under the law of Moses. Brought up to today, those are the religious ones, our people brought up under Christianity and Islam. “Hath not attained to the law of righteousness”: they did not understand the law in Christ.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law”: to get salvation, animal sacrifice. “For they stumbled at that stumblingstone”.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: “Behold, I lay in Sion a stumblingstone and rock of offence”: I lay in Israel a stumbling stone which is Christ, and he also is that rock of offence. “And whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.” Brothers and sisters, we ain’t gonna be ashamed. The Bible says we win at the end of all this; that’s what Romans 9 is explaining. But to win we must believe; we must prepare to win and expect to win.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: Who was Paul writing to in the book of Romans? Brothers hear the word Rome and fall off the horse, just like the Christian pastors.

“I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ”: Paul wished he could go through the same things Christ went through, “for my brethren”. Modern society teaches that everybody is one in Jesus, all brothers in Christ, the Arab man, the white man and the black man; yet the black man is always at the bottom. That is not what Paul is talking about. His brethren are “my kinsmen according to the flesh”, and that is how you get kinsmen: by sex.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

points: “Who are Israelites”: that clarifies it, crystal clear. The twelve tribes of Israel. To them pertain “the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants”, covenants with an s: the Old Testament and the New Testament are only for the Israelites. “The giving of the law” was given to the priests, and now under Christ we are all priests of the Most High; “and the service of God, and the promises”.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

points: “Of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came”: Christ came in the flesh through sex, the same way his brothers were made. There was no divine incarnation, also known today as the immaculate deception. There is no such thing in the Bible. “Who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.”

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

points: We talked about the wicked of our people that was born in vain; now we got to touch the other people. “Hath not the potter power over the clay”: the potter is the creator, the clay is the creation. “Of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?” Absolutely, because he’s the creator, he could do whatever he wants to do. He can choose Israel and despise every other nation; that’s up to him.

Everybody got a problem with that, everybody has an issue with the fact that God chose Israel and none else. Take it up with the Most High. Don’t get mad at us; we just the messengers. The Most High God of heaven and earth happened to choose his inheritance to be in Israel.

note.label: | SABBATH MORNING CLASS: When The Harvest Is Ripe

points: “What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”. That’s what this class is about: the harvest is ripening. It’s not ripe yet, but we almost there. He endured with much longsuffering. Fitted to destruction means he made a creation to be destroyed. That’s what he did.

note.label: | SABBATH MORNING CLASS: When The Harvest Is Ripe

points: “And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy”: the vessels of mercy are Israel, those who will receive mercy in the last days. He’ll have much longsuffering just to show all of his creation that at the end of the day, I choose who I want to choose; I’m the creator, I can do what I want to do. “Which he had afore prepared unto glory”. Y’all got to understand this thing: this was a fixed fight from the beginning.

note.label: | SABBATH MORNING CLASS: When The Harvest Is Ripe

points: “That he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory”. Afore means before: before time, in the past, he prepared them unto glory. Who did God afore prepare for glory? Israelites.

note.label: GENTILES: NORTHERN KINGDOM IN THE NEW TESTAMENT

points: “Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles”. Paul is saying even us, the same ones of afore time. Not of the Jews only, not of Judah, the southern kingdom, only, but also of the Gentiles.

What are the Jews called in the Old Testament? Judah: that is what Jews means. And who are the Gentiles in the Old Testament? Ephraim, the northern kingdom. So Jews is Judah and Gentiles is the northern kingdom. If you don’t understand this, the apologists are going to confound you, and you will get hemmed up and destroyed out there.

note.label: GENTILES: NORTHERN KINGDOM IN THE NEW TESTAMENT

points: “As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.” “In the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God.” Paul is quoting Hosea 1:10-11 regarding both the southern and the northern kingdom, Judah and Ephraim: the Jews of verse 24 are Judah, and the Gentiles of verse 24 are Ephraim, the northern kingdom.
They are called Gentiles here in Romans 9, and they are called strangers in 1 Peter 1.

note.label: GENTILES: NORTHERN KINGDOM IN THE NEW TESTAMENT

points: Paul is speaking: “Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth” All of this is possessive, still speaking about the same people.
“The adoption”: Christ adopting us into the covenant, the New Covenant, dying for the nation of Israel, as Matthew 1:21 says, he shall save his people, not everyone else.
“And the glory”: the kingdom of heaven, being exalted amongst all nations on this planet, pertains only to the Israelites.

“And the covenants”, plural. The old covenant belonged to Israel, plain and simple, and Hebrews 8:8 tells you the New Covenant belongs to Israel only. “And the giving of the law”: the law was only given to the Israelites. “And the service of God”: given to the Levites, and eventually to all Israel, because we are all kings and priests. “And the promises”: those pertain to Israel too. This whole chapter is talking about Israel.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

points: “Whose are the fathers”: Abraham. Abraham had many children, but who received the promise after him? Isaac. Isaac had two boys, and the promise went to Jacob. Jacob had 12 boys who received the promise, and we are the children of Jacob today: Jacob and Sons, never to be diminished, only replenished when Christ returns.

“And of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came”: Christ came out of an Israelite. “Who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.” Although we are living out these curses, they have an end. When Christ comes back there shall be no more curse, as Revelation says. But we have to do our due diligence in keeping God’s laws and teaching his word; we have to be faithful men, and fervent.
